title: LangChain 101
subtitle: Build, run, persist, and debug agents with LangChain 1.5, LangGraph 1.2, and Deep Agents 0.7, with a recorded answer for each decision
summary: How the LangChain Python stack turns a model, tools, and a prompt into an agent. The agent streams, pauses for approval, survives a crash, and leaves a trace. Every listing comes from an offline capture of langchain 1.5.0, langchain-core 1.8.0, langgraph 1.2.22, and deepagents 0.7.38. Every measured number comes from a recorded run on our own machines.
audience: You write Python and you have called a chat model API. You have read some LangChain code, maybe from the 0.x years. You want to know what the 1.x stack does before you build on it.

pin.subject: LangChain (Python): langchain, langchain-core, langgraph, deepagents, langsmith

outcomes: Install the stack from a lockfile on Python 3.11 or later, and say which package each import comes from.
Build an agent with create_agent, and predict each model call, tool call, and checkpoint of a run.
Choose a structured output strategy and a set of middleware, and predict the order in which their hooks run.
Stream a run in the mode you need, and keep a conversation across turns and restarts with a checkpointer.
Pause a run for human approval, resume it, and say which code runs again on the resume.
Count the attempts of each retry layer, and make a side effect safe when a crash replays it.
Connect MCP tools, a retriever, Deep Agents, and LangSmith tracing, and find the cause of a failure from its message.

palette.meaning: your code: the caller, its input, and its config
LangChain: create_agent, middleware, messages, and tools as objects
LangGraph: the graph, its nodes, the Pregel loop, and its streams
the chat model and each model call
tools and the results they return
services outside the process: providers, LangSmith, Ollama
lifecycle: steps, next nodes, interrupts, and resumes
durable state: checkpoints, stores, and their rows
failure: exceptions, error messages, and repeated side effects
outside LangChain: Python, packages, the machine, and the operator

plate.title: One invoke, two model calls, one tool call
plate.caption: The agent from the capture kit answers `What is 2 + 3?` with two model calls and one tool call. The checkpointer saves five checkpoints on the thread. From capture/out/06-agent-run.txt, capture/out/28-checkpoint-memory.txt, and capture/out/30-state-history-forks.txt.

parts.title: LangChain on One Page
parts.thesis: Four projects share one name, and one agent run passes through three of them before it returns.
parts.summary: What LangChain, LangGraph, LangSmith, and Deep Agents each do, and their claims beside our results. Then one create_agent run from invoke to the last checkpoint.

parts.title: Start
parts.thesis: Install from a lockfile on Python 3.11, then learn the four objects that every agent is made of: the model, the messages, the tools, and the prompt.
parts.summary: The package map and the install, init_chat_model and model profiles, messages and content blocks, tools with ToolRuntime and their errors, and the system prompt.

parts.title: Agents
parts.thesis: create_agent compiles a graph, and its structured output strategy and its middleware decide what each run sends, retries, and blocks.
parts.summary: The graph that create_agent builds, and the three structured output strategies with their failure rates. Then middleware hooks and their order, the 19 built-in classes, retry layers and backup models, PII, and the beta decision middleware.

parts.title: Streaming and Memory
parts.thesis: A run streams its steps as they happen, and a checkpointer and a store keep its state, so you must know what each one yields, saves, repeats, and gives back.
parts.summary: Stream modes and stream_events v3, checkpointers and threads, durability and crashes, stores and namespaces, summarization and checkpoint growth, and what serialization gives back.

parts.title: LangGraph and Control
parts.thesis: A LangGraph run is state, reducers, and steps, and you control it by pausing, resuming, replaying, forking, nesting, and limiting those steps.
parts.summary: StateGraph and reducers, Send and Command, and the functional API. Then interrupts, human review, time travel, subgraphs, and the error handlers and limits of a node.

parts.title: Integrations
parts.thesis: Retrieval, MCP, Deep Agents, and LangSmith each plug into create_agent, and each one adds a cost or a failure that you must know before you rely on it.
parts.summary: Retrievers and vector stores, MCP tools through langchain.mcp, Deep Agents 0.7 and its token cost, LangSmith tracing, and evaluation without an account.

parts.title: Operate and Debug
parts.thesis: Running an agent for other people adds a server, a bill, attackers, old code, and failures at night, and each one has a recorded answer.
parts.summary: Agent Server under langgraph dev, up, and deploy, and the cost of each layer against a plain SDK loop. Then security at five boundaries, migration from 0.x, a table of symptoms, and the limits of this edition.

parts.title: Build
parts.thesis: Four small programs on a local model and one offline drill show what to build around LangChain, and which failures come from the model and which from the code.
parts.summary: A SQL agent with approved writes, a retrieval agent with sources, and an assistant that survives a restart. Then a deep agent with a subagent, and a drill for seven failures.

reference.title: Reference
reference.thesis: The parameters, hooks, stream events, persistence methods, variables, errors, terms, sources, and figures of this manual, in one place.
reference.summary: Lookup tables for create_agent, middleware, streams, persistence, environment variables, and errors. Then a glossary, the sources and conflicts, the figure index, and how the manual was made.
